question: By which concept are the Mughal style of gardens in India inspired ?

options.text: The Persian idea of paradise gardens

solution:
The correct answer is __**The Persian idea of paradise gardens**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The Mughal style of gardens in India was heavily influenced by the **Persian concept of paradise gardens**, known as "Charbagh." These gardens were designed to represent the Islamic vision of paradise, often described as a lush, symmetrical garden divided by water channels.
 
• The Persian Charbagh design divides the garden into four quadrants with pathways and flowing water. This layout symbolizes the four rivers of paradise as mentioned in the **Quran**, representing water, milk, honey, and wine.
